name: Silver Key Senior Apartments
headline: Silver Key Senior Apartments (Silver Key Apartments at South Murray) is a 50-home, all income-restricted building for adults 62+ in southeast Colorado Springs, with 13 VASH homes for older homeless veterans, sponsored by nonprofit Silver Key Senior Services with turnkey developer MGL Partners; it won a 2022 Round One federal 9% award and opened in late 2024.
why_it_matters: It shows a service-provider nonprofit using its own land (sold in with seller carryback), VASH vouchers and on-campus services to get a first 9% deal built and fully leased in about three months, a template it is now repeating at North Weber.

status.label: Built and occupied (move-ins from November 2024)
status.detail: Groundbreaking was 2023-09-22; residents began moving in at the start of November 2024 and the public ribbon cutting was 2024-12-04. Silver Key's 2026 application says the building was fully leased in three months. No placed-in-service or 8609 record was found online.

next_step: Watch for CHFA compliance or placed-in-service records; Silver Key's second deal (North Weber, 2026 award) is the follow-on.

key_numbers.meaning: 48 one-bedroom and 2 two-bedroom homes; 13 reserved for older homeless veterans with VASH vouchers.
About $13.1M over 10 years; no state credit is shown on the award report.
13 homes at 30% AMI, 10 at 40%, 13 at 50% and 14 at 60%.
Application budget of $17,673,061, including $3.01M of Division of Housing gap funds.

background.text: Silver Key bought the land in 2017 and owns it free and clear; it planned to sell it into the tax-credit partnership at appraised value with seller carryback financing while keeping full ownership of the general partner.
An earlier tax-credit application was for 70 units; Silver Key cut it to 50, hired MGL as turnkey developer, added a second access through its campus and added 13 VASH homes.
The City Planning Commission unanimously approved the multifamily conditional use on 2022-01-20, and the city gave the project Rapid Response certification to speed entitlements.
Because Silver Key is a nonprofit serving seniors, the application expected a statutory property tax exemption.
The market study's overall (26.2%) and 50% AMI (32%) capture rates were above CHFA guidelines; the application relied on low vacancies and waiting lists at existing senior properties.
Silver Key pledged half of cash flow for five years, plus Medicaid, Older Americans Act and VA funds, to pay for services for the VASH residents.
Silver Key received more than 550 applications for the 50 homes; residents began moving in at the start of November 2024.

discrepancies.text: CHFA, the Gazette and KOAA give the address as 1575 S. Murray Blvd., while KKTV placed the apartments at 1625 S. Murray Blvd., which the Gazette identifies as Silver Key's headquarters next door.
The application budgeted $17,673,061, while the Gazette's opening story refers to a $14.7 million project (inferred to mean this complex from the article's context).
